_authoring_conventions.note: Same conventions as fixtures/cinderella — see fixtures/authoring-notes.md. This package is original, written for this repository; nothing in it is adapted from an existing work.
_authoring_conventions.entry_state_and_exit_state: { <entity_id>: { <column>: <value>, ... }, ... } — one object per touched entity, naming only the core columns this scene asserts.
_authoring_conventions.new_rows_in_exit_state: Reserved keys _new_relationships / _new_character_knowledge, using the same row shape as world_model_seed.
_authoring_conventions.why_this_fixture_exists: Four scenes, so a whole live telling costs four writer requests rather than fourteen (AGENTS.md, The Gemini API key). It is deliberately short enough to read in one sitting and re-run after an edit.
_authoring_conventions.volitional_assertion: scene_02 asserts rel_003.sentiment, a V-tier column. The author asserting a volitional column goes through the same authority the engine does (ADR 0005), so at author-time it lands in the proposals queue rather than committing — which is what gives the scene compile view something real to resolve without a live model call.
_authoring_conventions.characters_present_includes_the_absent: scene_01 lists char_marchetti though she is not in the teahouse: characters_present is what the deterministic join reads, so a character a beat names but the list omits reaches the writer as a name with no World Model row behind it, which the compiler reports as missing_fact.

characters.name: Vess Kalloway
characters.goal: one clean score and out of the trade

bag.tell: counts under her breath when the timing gets tight
bag.cover: presents as a buyer's agent from out of town

bag.note: has brought Vess every job she has taken for nine years
shows the collection once a year and never lends from it
keeps the guard roster by the gallery clock because Marchetti told him to

bag.description: back booth, bad light, the only room in the city where Dace will talk business
one long room of glass cases, loud with money once a year
behind the gallery, one door, one stand in the middle of it
runs from the vault-room landing down to the alley door
wet, empty, one block from the gallery's alley door
a palm-sized cat of Baltic amber, seated, with one eye chipped away
Vess's copy, cast and tinted over five weeks

bag.note: Marchetti's father set it; she will not have it touched

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Set the job, the mark, and the one small fact the last scene will turn on — laid down flat, among other facts, so it does not announce itself.
required_beats: Dace lays out the job: Ilsa Marchetti's amber cat, out of the vault room, on the one night a year the gallery is open
Vess has already made the copy and has it wrapped in her coat
Dace mentions in passing that the gallery clock has run four minutes fast since Marchetti's father set it, and that she will not have it touched
Vess takes the job and goes; Dace will wait on Ferrier Street
scene_cards.tone: low-lit and transactional; two people who have done this a dozen times and still like each other
invariants: Vess never says out loud what the copy is for
the clock is mentioned as gossip about Marchetti, not as a plan

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Put Vess inside, get her the key, and start the clock on Brannan noticing her — the pressure the rest of the story runs on.
required_beats: Vess works the room as a buyer's agent and gets Marchetti talking about the cat and the eye it is missing
Brannan looks at Vess twice, and the second time he does not look away first
Vess takes the service-stair key off Brannan's belt while he is turned toward the champagne, and counts under her breath doing it
scene_cards.tone: bright, crowded, teeth behind every smile
invariants: Marchetti never leaves the gallery floor

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The job itself, done clean and fast — and the flaw in it, which Vess sees and takes anyway.
required_beats: the service stair takes Vess up to the vault-room door with the gala still loud underneath her
she puts the resin cat on the stand and the amber cat in her coat, and it takes eleven seconds
the copy's chipped eye is on the right; the real one is chipped on the left, and there was never time to recast it
invariants: Vess is alone in the vault room
she does not fix the eye and does not pretend to herself that it will pass a second look

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Collect both plants at once: the clock buys the gap she walks out through, and the eye sets the clock running on how long the score stays clean.
required_beats: the guard rotation comes four minutes early because Brannan keeps the roster by the gallery clock, and Vess is on the stair inside that gap
she passes Brannan on the landing and puts the key back on his belt going by, and he lets her pass because by his watch the stair is covered
on Ferrier Street Dace asks whether it is clean, and Vess tells him they have until somebody looks at the cat from the left
scene_cards.tone: fast, then flat; the win and the cost arriving in the same breath
invariants: the story ends on the street, not in the gallery

voice_card.narrative_distance: tight on Vess; the reader knows what she notices and nothing she does not
voice_card.register: flat, unsentimental, wry under pressure; competence described as work rather than flair
voice_card.sentence_rhythm: short sentences, hard stops, the occasional long one that runs when she is moving
imagery_palette: the weight of a coat pocket
voice_card.dialogue_density: high; people say less than they mean and the narration does not explain it
voice_card.style_exemplar: The clock had been wrong for thirty years, and everybody in the building had built their evening around it.
